items.title: Today's lesson
items.content:
A boy panting with a **cramp** after a race and a bowl of dough that has **risen** overnight open the lesson: how do cells get energy from food, with and without oxygen?

A **lime-water test** and one flow chart show the three fates of **pyruvate** and compare **aerobic** with **anaerobic** respiration.

Air is followed from the nostrils to the **alveoli**, and a fish's **gills** show why breathing in water must be faster.

Some pictures have an **animation as picture 2**: show picture 1, ask, then click › to play it.

items.title: You already know
items.content:
• digestion ends with glucose absorbed into the blood

• cytoplasm and mitochondria of a cell

• lime water turns milky with carbon dioxide

• diffusion: substances move from where there is more of them to where there is less

items.title: By the end, you can
items.content:
**1.** Compare aerobic and anaerobic respiration.

**2.** Describe the different fates of pyruvate in mitochondria, muscle cells and yeast.

**3.** Describe the human respiratory system and gas exchange in the alveoli.

**4.** Explain why terrestrial animals breathe more slowly than aquatic animals, and the role of haemoglobin.

chunks.name: A cramp and a risen dough

items.text:
**What this shows**

Left: a boy has just finished a race; he is **panting** and holding his **thigh**.

**Answer to Question 1**

Take guesses and leave it open. His muscles needed more oxygen than he could breathe in, so they made **lactic acid**, which causes the cramp; breathing hard brings in the extra oxygen (Parts 1 and 2).

**What this shows**

Right: a bowl of dough, made with **yeast**, has **doubled in size** overnight.

**Answer to Question 2**

Take guesses and leave it open. The **yeast** broke down sugar in the dough **without oxygen** and gave out **carbon dioxide** (Parts 1 and 2).

**Answer to Question 4**

items.prompt: Fill in the blanks: Pyruvate is a ______-carbon molecule, made in the ______ of the cell.
A sealed bottle of grape juice with a little yeast bulges after a few days and smells of alcohol. The process and its two products are
options: aerobic respiration: carbon dioxide and water

items.text:
**On this question**

**A**: **three**; **cytoplasm**. Glucose has six carbons; pyruvate is made in the cytoplasm, before the mitochondria.

**On this question**

**A**: **fermentation** (anaerobic respiration by yeast): **ethanol** (the alcohol smell) and **carbon dioxide** (makes the bottle bulge).

items.prompt: Why does aerobic respiration release much more energy than anaerobic respiration from the same amount of glucose?
options: Glucose is broken down completely to carbon dioxide and water
It happens only in the cytoplasm

items.text:
**On this question**

**(a)**: lactic acid builds up in the muscles and causes the cramp.

**On this question**

**A**: in aerobic respiration glucose is broken down **completely**; in anaerobic respiration much of the energy stays in the **ethanol or lactic acid**.

items.prompt: In this respiratory system, in which part are gases exchanged, and which part has rings of cartilage?
In a lung disease, the walls between many small alveoli break down, leaving fewer, larger sacs. Why does the person feel breathless?
options: Surface area for gas exchange falls

items.text:
**On this question**

**A**: gases are exchanged in the **alveoli, F**; the **trachea, B**, has the rings of cartilage. All the parts: A nasal passage, B trachea, C bronchus, D lung, E diaphragm, F alveoli.

**On this question**

**A**: fewer, larger sacs have less total **surface area**, so less oxygen diffuses into the blood.

items.text:
**Step 1: picture 1, then click ›**

How much oxygen is in 1 litre of air and in 1 litre of water? Students guess first. **After Question 13, click ›** to show the bars: about 210 mL against about 6 mL.

**Answer to Question 13**

**Step 2.** Water holds **far less oxygen** than air, so an aquatic animal must pass a lot of water over its gills, quickly, to get enough. Land animals breathe oxygen-rich air, so they breathe **more slowly**. Then click › on the chart.

**Step 3**

Read the key idea: large animals need a **respiratory pigment**, **haemoglobin**, to carry oxygen.

**Answer to Question 14**

**Step 4.** Less oxygen reaches the cells, so less energy is released: the person feels **tired and breathless**.

items.prompt: What advantage does a land animal have over an aquatic animal in getting oxygen for respiration?
options: Air contains much more oxygen than water
Water contains more oxygen than air
Land animals do not need oxygen

items.prompt: Why does oxygen need haemoglobin to be carried in our blood, but carbon dioxide does not?
options: Oxygen dissolves poorly in water; carbon dioxide is more soluble
Carbon dioxide is heavier than oxygen
Oxygen is made in the blood

items.text:
**On this question**

**A**: air contains **much more oxygen** than the same volume of water, so a land animal gets enough while breathing more slowly.

**On this question**

**A**: oxygen dissolves **poorly**, so too little would travel dissolved; carbon dioxide is **more soluble**, so most of it travels dissolved in the blood.
